heroHeadline: Fall Weather Deepens the De-Escalation: NW Ontario's Active Count Hits Season-Low 30, First Nations Evacuees Fall to 178
heroSubtitle: Canada's wildfire season continued its steady fall retreat: Northwestern Ontario's active fire count dropped to 30 by Sept 15 — the region's lowest of the season — down from 62 on Sept 3, with no new fires confirmed all week and the fire danger rating falling to low across most of the Northwest Region. The Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34/35) remains not under control but with activity staying low. Nationally, the human toll of the season has eased sharply on the Indigenous Services Canada evacuation dashboard: just 17 First Nations communities remained impacted by wildfire as of Sept 14 (16 in BC, one each in Saskatchewan and Ontario), with 5 under active evacuation and 178 individuals displaced — down from 4,294 evacuees across 25 communities on Aug 18. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or fire starts were identified this cycle.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
